source.title: In Search of Probeable Generalization Measures
source.authors: Jonathan Jaegerman; Khalil Damouni; M. S. Hosseini; K. Plataniotis

record.tranche_reason: The study measures associations between weight-derived metrics and train–test generalization gap using different measures from V7; it does not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.gate_note: The study reports correlations and qualitative trends between its own weight-derived quality metrics and generalization gap. NATS-Bench figure values are not stated numerically in the text; no specific values are inferred from figures. Results from supplementary figures are not available in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study measures correlations between weight-derived rank or norm metrics and generalization performance. It never measures magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or compares its ranking with other measures, so it does not test V7. Varying widths and optimizers supplies model families for metric evaluation, without reporting the comparisons required by V2 or V4. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: effective rank and stable quality are useful and comparatively robust across the tested GenProb variations, but the investigated measures are sensitive to drastic architectural changes. The two-dataset limitation describes GenProb; preliminary NATS-Bench experiments additionally include ImageNet-16-120.
record.recipe_differences: Measures weight-derived quality metrics and their correlations with generalization gap; does not apply V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation sharpness method.
record.method_sensitivity: Search-space architecture changes the reported correlations; correlations vary over training stages, datasets, and low-rank-factorization preprocessing.

fits_no_version.finding: Effective rank, stable quality and weight norms correlate with generalization performance to varying degrees. Correlations depend on architecture, training stage and preprocessing; effective rank and stable quality perform best in the reported GenProb comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Probeable weight-derived rank and quality metrics can track generalization performance within related convolutional model families, with reliability depending on architecture, training stage and preprocessing.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning and Applications (2021)
record.problems: The supplied text gives mostly qualitative descriptions of correlations, with plotted values not transcribed. It reports simple convolutional networks and two datasets in GenProb; the authors note that the measures do not prove robust to drastic architecture variations. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported correlations.
record.rows_left_out: None of the available text results were left out. Supplementary figures are referenced but not included in the supplied text, so their individual plotted results were not extracted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out performance compared with natural-label generalization under the same training recipe.
Test-error changes with widening beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning budgets and recovery recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes that remove the penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization or augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: T2 is inappropriate because replacing sharpness with rank or norm metrics changes the property being tested. The cannot_determine states reflect inability to assess a listed version, rather than uncertainty about whether the reported metric correlations exist.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization, natural-label generalization, and held-out accuracy versus chance.
Whether widening beyond the interpolation threshold continues to lower test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptive recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Effects of removing memorized training examples.

rows.subject: NATS-Bench models (aggregate across models in size search space)
rows.operation_detail: Spearman correlations of quality metrics with generalization gap
rows.measure: Spearman correlation between quality metrics and generalization gap
rows.value: Several measures reach to and above 0.9
rows.note: Aggregate statement about several measures; the text does not assign the stated correlation magnitude to individual measures or datasets.
rows.check: These correlations do not measure any claim version. Table II specifies 12 and 90 epochs for the size search space, not 200. The stated correlations reaching or exceeding 0.9 summarize test accuracy and generalization gap together; the text does not identify which individual gap correlations reach that level.

rows.operation_detail: Spearman correlations of quality metrics with generalization gap
rows.measure: Spearman correlation between quality metrics and generalization gap
rows.note: Aggregate statement; the text says patterns from the size search space do not appear for the topology search space.
rows.check: These correlations do not measure any claim version. Table II specifies 12 and 200 epochs for the topology search space, not 90. The correlation ceiling summarizes both performance targets rather than identifying individual gap correlations.

rows.subject: ResNet34
rows.stage_stated: trained with AdaS; weights saved at every epoch
rows.operation_detail: Tracked quality metrics and generalization gap through training

conditions.value: until completion; weights saved every epoch

rows.measure: Whether quality metrics mirror generalization gap
rows.value: Stable quality and effective rank begin mirroring the generalization gap at around 10 epochs; Frobenius and spectral norm measures only begin at the 60th epoch
rows.note: The paper reports qualitative timing, not correlation values, for these training trajectories.
rows.check: Metric tracking does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness. The timing statement concerns raw metrics; LRF improves earlier tracking, although norm measures retain a distinct decline between epochs 10 and 60. Combining preprocessing conditions obscures this distinction.

rows.subject: GenProb models trained with Adam (aggregate across models)
rows.operation_detail: Related effective rank to generalization gap
rows.measure: Relationship between effective rank and generalization gap
rows.value: Clear linear relationship at later epochs; trends with generalization gap show at epoch 40
rows.note: Aggregate across the plotted family of models; precise correlation values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: The effective-rank relationship does not measure any version. Preserve the authors' negative generalization-gap convention when interpreting its direction.

rows.subject: GenProb models (aggregate across models)
rows.operation_detail: Compared quality-measure correlations with generalization gap
rows.measure: Correlation of quality metrics with generalization gap
rows.value: Some correlations approach 1; correlations with generalization gap plateau after 40 epochs; low-rank factorization decreases correlation magnitude through all stages
rows.locator: Section V.C; Fig. 5(c), Fig. 5(d), Supplementary Material Fig. 41-42
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative description; the text does not state per-metric correlation values here.
rows.check: These correlations do not measure any version. Figure 5(c–d) concerns Adam; results should not be generalized to all seven optimizers from the supplied text. The near-one correlation statement summarizes both test accuracy and gap, without specifying individual gap coefficients.

rows.subject: GenProb models (aggregate across models)
rows.operation_detail: Compared quality metrics' generalization-gap correlations across metrics and datasets
rows.measure: Relative correlation of metrics with generalization gap
rows.value: Effective rank and stable quality are described as the most effective and robust; Frobenius and spectral norm underperform consistently and are less consistent across dataset complexities
rows.note: Aggregate comparison across training phases and dataset complexities; no individual correlation values are stated.
rows.check: Ranking effective rank, stable quality and norm metrics does not test V7's ranking of magnitude-aware sharpness. The weaker norm correlations cannot establish a partial sharpness effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
